title: He was a king…
paragraphs:
He was a king…
but couldn’t control the war inside his own mind.

And the one thing that calmed him?
Was something he never learned to carry himself.

Saul had authority—but no peace.
A throne—but no rest.
Power in public… torment in private.

Scripture doesn’t hide it.
In 1 Samuel 16:14, it says the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and a distressing spirit troubled him.

The real crisis wasn’t the demon.
It was the distance.
And here’s the part we don’t like to admit—

You can look anointed…
and still be empty.

You can lead people…
and still be losing yourself.

You can sit in church…
and still be spiritually suffocating.
Because some of you know exactly what that feels like.

You worship publicly…
but secretly, your thoughts are loud, restless, unclean.

You pray occasionally…
but obedience is delayed.

You say “God is first”…
but your habits say otherwise.
And the silence is getting heavier.
Saul needed David to do what Saul himself refused to become.
Every time David played, Scripture says in 1 Samuel 16:23 that relief came to Saul, and the torment left him.

You don’t just need deliverance…
you need restored intimacy.

Because what you carry in private
will always manifest in public.

If peace only comes when someone else is leading you into God’s presence…
you’ve stopped walking with Him yourself.

This is deeper than stress.
Deeper than mood swings.

This is what happens when calling is maintained…
but connection is neglected.

Some people don’t need a breakthrough.
They need repentance.

Not louder worship songs.
Not more distractions.
Because the issue was never that God stopped being present.
It’s that Saul stopped honoring Him.

When was the last time you sat with God
without rushing?

When was the last time you obeyed immediately
instead of negotiating?

When was the last time your worship was real…
not routine?
Because delayed obedience is still disobedience.
And hidden compromise always grows louder over time.
But here’s where grace walks in—
God didn’t leave Saul without a witness.

And today—
He’s sending you this.

Because the same God who allowed David’s harp to calm a tormented king
sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to do something far greater.
The Bible says in Romans 3:23 that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.

That includes you.
That includes me.
Because in Romans 5:8, God shows His love—while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you cleaned up.
Jesus didn’t just play a song over your pain.
So now the invitation isn’t “try harder.”
Restore the relationship you’ve been replacing with routine.
Because you were never created to survive off borrowed worship.
You were created to walk with God.

You are not a spiritually exhausted performer.
You are a called, redeemed child of God.
Because 1 John 1:9 promises—if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
This isn’t the end of your story.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
We’re going deeper into why some people feel God less… even when they’re doing more.
